items.text: If normal system air pressure is low ie 20 kgf/cm² or more, a start may be attempted and the pressure built up on the compressor before taxy. Otherwise, the system must be charged via the external connector, as must the emergency system.

items.text: The rear magneto switch should remain OFF until priming has been completed but must be placed to 1+2 (ON) before attempting to start. On British registered aircraft the flap and undercarriage selectors in the rear cockpit are locked in Neutral.

items.text: Priming: Cold = 8 pumps set to CYL with the propeller pulled through one blade per pump. 2 pumps set to CARB. Hot = Up to 4 pumps on CYL. A warm engine must not be pulled through. All pulling through must be in the direction of rotation.
The engine is considered sufficiently warm when the oil temperature = 40ºC and CHT = 120ºC.

items.text: Vacate aircraft, fitting control locks as appropriate. Drain the air system water trap after each flight. If a/c is to be left overnight, consider fitting covers.
As no oxygen system is fitted, the aircraft is limited to a maximum height of 10,000ft.
Maximum weight for all flight regimes 1315kg (2899 lb)
All aerobatic manoeuvres are permitted. Aerobatics are not to be attempted with landing gear or flaps extended. Both canopies must be closed and locked.
2 minutes maximum with 3 minutes erect before next period of inverted flight.
Take-off power is limited to a maximum of 5 minutes
Maximum RPM is limited to a maximum of 1 minute

Maximum flight range at a height of 1640ft (500m) and an airspeed of 210-215km/h (113-116kt) at 1315kg AUW (119 litres fuel) with 10% unusable fuel supply in 'Cruise 2' engine running condition is 510km (275nm). In this case the flight duration is approximately 2 hours 45 minutes
No engine fire extinguisher is fitted

items.response: Try to keep flames away from the cockpit
Release to enable the aircraft to be pushed away from burning fuel on the ground

items.text: If fire/smoke has occurred shortly after an electrical switch has been moved
items.response: Reselect the particular switch to former position

items.text: If fire/smoke persists: All non essential electrics OFF.
If visible signs of fire: Land as soon as possible or, if parachutes are worn, abandon the aircraft.

items.response: Dive and sideslip to keep the flames away from the cockpit

items.text: If the fire goes out land as soon as possible at the nearest airfield; be prepared for a higher stalling speed if the aircraft skin is damaged.
If the fire persists, land as soon as possible or, if parachutes are worn, abandon the aircraft.

If possible maintain a speed of not less than 160km/h and lower the flaps as required. If time permits before landing, turn off the fuel and switch off the ignition. Tighten the harness and open the canopy.
Proceed as for engine failure on take-off. The best gliding speed is 160km/h with the flaps up.

Make the initial approach at 160km/h with flaps up; open the canopy at 50m. Lower the flaps only when certain of getting into the selected landing area, and aim to cross the boundary at 160km/h with full flap or with flaps up. At low speeds the rate of descent is very high.

items.response: Release. Ensure parachute harness not released

items.text: The pilot should bale out first, the rear seat occupant following once the pilot is clear of the aircraft. When baling out, endeavour to dive downwards and away from the aircraft to try to avoid hitting the tailplane. The aeroplane may be abandoned to either side or inverted.
No ditching experience has been obtained for this aircraft, but the following is a general guide.

items.response: Tail first at as low an air speed as possible
Reselect ON briefly to permit use of the radio and electrical circuits for limited period
CARB, operate to maintain fuel pressure
Idle, advance slowly, if rough running remains set 72% to clear plugs
Verify DOWN, three greens and mech. indication

items.text: If the undercarriage fails to lower on the emergency system or insufficient air pressure is available the a/c must be landed wheels UP. Do NOT retract the U/C after lowering on the emergency system. Do not close the emerg. air tap until after the engine shut down on landing.
A flapless approach and landing must be carried out. The approach speed being 160-170 km/h. The flare and the landing roll will be correspondingly longer.

If the “Borings in Oil” light illuminates in flight consideration must be given to landing as soon as possible, as this could mean the engine oil contaminated with metallic particles and a potential engine failure.
